items.q: Painless progressive arcuate field loss with cupped disc and open angles is which disease?
items.exp: Chronic outflow failure excavates silently; prostaglandin led therapy with target pressures preserves remaining nerve while fields monitor. Cataract instead glares with cloudy lens.
items.kp: Quiet tunnel vision with big cup: open angle.

items.q: First line medical therapy for primary open angle glaucoma is which class and caution?
o: Prostaglandin analogue (latanoprost) at night; irreversible iris darkening and lash growth
items.exp: Once nightly dosing with strong efficacy leads guidelines; heterochromia and hypertrichosis counselled while asthma and bradycardia instead forbid timolol first. Laser trabeculoplasty rivals drops initially.
items.kp: Night drop darkening iris: prostaglandin first.

items.q: Severe eye pain with halos, vomiting, hazy cornea and mid dilated pupil after movie in dark indicates what?
o: Acute angle closure needing emergency pressure lowering then bilateral iridotomy
items.exp: Darkness dilates pushing bulky iris over trabeculum in short hypermetropic eyes; acetazolamide, mannitol and pilocarpine bridge to definitive laser holes in both eyes. Migraine lacks rock hard globe.
items.kp: Dark room pain with halos: shut angle.

items.q: Definitive anatomical cure for pupillary block angle closure is what?
items.exp: Iridotomy equalises chambers flattening iris from trabeculum; fellow eye prophylaxis prevents sequential blindness. Lenses extract in crowded or phacomorphic variants.
r: Incorrect. Lens removal helps crowded eyes.
items.kp: Block at pupil: hole the iris, both sides.

items.q: Timolol eye drops are contraindicated or cautioned in which patients?
o: Asthmatics and bradycardic or heart block patients
items.exp: Systemic beta blockade wheezes and slows; ask lungs and pulse before prescribing while masking hypoglycaemia in brittle diabetics. Once daily gel preparations still absorb systemically.
r: Correct. Lungs and slow hearts beware.

items.q: Nasal step on visual fields in glaucoma represents what?
o: Arcuate bundle defect respecting horizontal midline from nerve fibre loss
items.exp: Superior and inferior arcuate fibres die first sparing midline; Bjerrum and ring scotomas extend the same bundle logic toward tunnel vision. Neurological defects instead respect vertical meridian.
items.kp: Step at nasal midline: arcuate fibres dying.

items.q: Trabeculectomy bleb with late redness, pain and vision drop after years suggests what?
o: Bleb related endophthalmitis needing emergency antibiotics and vitrectomy assessment
items.exp: Thin avascular blebs leak and seed streptococci years on; leaking blebs with cells need admission, tap and intensive therapy while prophylactic repair debates continue. Lifelong bleb vigilance counselled.
items.kp: Old filter bleb gone red and sore: infected.

items.q: Normal tension glaucoma differs from primary open angle chiefly by what management?
o: Damage despite normal pressures needing even lower targets with vascular workup
items.exp: Disc haemorrhages and vascular dysregulation (migraine, Raynaud, sleep apnoea) accompany; pressure still lowers (drops, laser, surgery) toward single digits or low teens. Progression monitored identically.
items.kp: Cupping at normal pressure: aim lower still.

items.q: Pilocarpine relieves angle closure by which mechanism and limits use how?
o: Miosis pulling iris from angle with brow ache, myopia and retinal detachment caution
items.exp: Sphincter constriction thins peripheral iris opening trabeculum once pressure permits response; chronic use clouds lens and tugs retina in myopes. Definitive iridotomy follows.
items.kp: Pinpoint pupil opening drain but aching brow: pilocarpine.

items.q: Steroid induced glaucoma arises through which mechanism and needs what?
o: Trabecular outflow resistance from steroid response; stop or switch steroids with pressure control
items.exp: Responders (myopes, POAG families, children) clog meshwork within weeks of potent drops; scheduled pressure monitoring catches rises while fluorometholone or ciclosporin substitutes disease control.
